parole.testo: Dictionnaire du faisceau dialectal arabe andalou thinks this is borrowed from Egyptian ꜣṯt (“bed”). This view is amenable since all other terms in the root can be understood as being secondary to the present noun.

parole.significato: Ra, the Egyptian god of the Sun.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Egyptian r:a-ra (rꜥ, “the sun; Ra”).

An ancient borrowing of Egyptian r(ꜣ)-pr (“temple”), due to agricultural properties (i.e., lands) in Egypt—which Bedouins roamed—having been administered by temples. The similarity to Akkadian 𒊑𒅁𒄣 (ri-ip-qu /⁠ripqu⁠/, “field broken up for cultivation”) is coincidental.

Borrowed from Egyptian sḫt (“field, open country”). Unrelated to سَاحَ (sāḥa, “to travel”) if that sense as opposed to “to run, to melt” is not denominal from the present noun. Compare رِيف (rīf, “countryside, rural land”) also borrowed from Egyptian.

parole.significato: to smell, to explore by odour
